points.description: Defines DHCP: a network management protocol (used in IP networks) in which a server dynamically assigns IP addresses and/or other network configuration parameters (e.g. DNS server, netmask, default gateway) to devices/hosts on the network. Equivalent wording accepted.

levels.says: Says only that DHCP is a protocol that assigns IP addresses, with no mention of dynamic/automatic assignment by a server or of other configuration parameters.

points.description: States a use/purpose: it simplifies installation and configuration of end systems/hosts by automatically (or manually) assigning IP addresses and providing extra configuration information such as DNS server, netmask, default router. Any one such valid use earns the marks; mentioning that it replaced RARP/BOOTP alone is not enough.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a definition of DHCP as a protocol where a server dynamically assigns IP addresses/configuration parameters, plus a stated use such as simplifying host configuration or supplying DNS/netmask/gateway. Part marks: a vague definition (just assigns IP addresses) earns half of the definition point. No marks for unrelated definitions.
